script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for June 30. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Touch metal and wood in the same room—the metal feels colder.  But they're the same temperature.  What you're actually feeling isn't temperature; it's how fast heat leaves your hand.

Atoms and molecules are always moving—vibrating, spinning, bouncing. Temperature measures how energetically they're dancing. At absolute zero, motion would stop. At high temperatures, molecules move frantically. Metal feels colder than wood because metal conducts heat away from your hand faster.  Both are room temperature, but metal steals your heat quickly, wood slowly.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Energy flows from more to less.  Temperature teaches that understanding direction helps you work with natural forces.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Heat Awareness - Feel the Flow.

Here's your activity: Pay attention to heat flow today: your warm coffee cooling, cold drinks warming, your body heat escaping outdoors. Feel how different materials conduct heat differently. Understanding heat flow helps you stay comfortable with less energy. This helps you notice heat transfer in daily life.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about how hot and cold work can be applied to heat awareness - feel the flow. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
